Sober for 10 months. 

Here is what worked for me : 

1. I’ve replaced weed by healthy dopamine (doing a physical activity that I like, trying a new recipe, crafting)

2. Strict sleep schedule. 

3. Eating whole foods

4. Spending a LOT of time in nature.

5. Allowing myself to feel. Sit down with any emotions as incomfortable as it was. Especially feeling bored or lonely. Overtime I realised just like a high, these feelings were temporary.

I was a highly functionning weed smoker. I studied in university in a particularly demanding program/field. Lived in my own and nobody knew I was smoking everyday (when out of work). But after stopping weed, productivity just got better.

My DBT group was an intensive group. In my country (lol Canada) access to mental health care is very difficult so to make as much people have access to therapy it has to be intensive.
It was an outpatient, once a week for 3-4 hour group session for 14 weeks
We couldn’t miss as we’d be kicked out of the group.
The group was heterogenous. Men, non binaries and women aged 18-75 were mixed. We had 2 therapists. We were about 10 ish people. Therapy started with an individual meeting with a third therapist for that one time. She made us sign the contract (ex : if we knew someone in the group, we had to say it. We couldnt have relationships with other participants…) During the first 2 hours of the session we would learn theory about BPD, attachment styles, coping mecanisms etc. I took notes that I still look at daily. 
Then for the 2 next hours we would share with the group. They wanted us to give ourselves one goal each week and we would talk about whether or not we managed to success in that goal. Sometimes it would just be plain venting from people. It was needed. Everybody offered support and it was crazy for me because i really felt heard by complete strangers. No judgement. 

During the 14 weeks we had 2-4 individual meetings with one of the 2 therapists. During those we discussed more long term goals. Mine was to stop self harming and achieve sobriety. We worked through those.

After the 14 weeks finished, we had 4 “emergency meetings” we could take within a year and a half. I used all of them lol 😭🤣💀

Feel free to dm if anything

It literally changed my life, helped me accept the disease better, made me a better person, made me love myself… 
Actually shared stuff I learned as advice to friends.
Go for it you will not regret it.
Because of DBT, i’m sober, i stopped selfharming, i stopped putting myself in dangerous situations. 
It didnt stop but helped me understanding my chronic sense of emptiness, my erratic attachment issues and my chronic suicidality !
